reasons.text: Buys feedstock inside a closed loop of 5 recyclers trading the same material (39% of its feedstock)
Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 97% of months
36% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
Uploaded plant photos are near-duplicates of photos registered by 1 other plant(s)
Electricity bought is only 0.45x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (134 kWh/t against at least 300)
48% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity

inspection_checklist: Trace the material flow between the plants in the loop (weighbridge slips, vehicle GPS); the same tonnes may be invoiced round a ring.
Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Compare the plant against the entities sharing its identifiers (bank, address, director, photos); consider a joint inspection.
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
